property_summary: For any caller and any sent value, after go() completes the contract's entire ether balance is forwarded to the originally-deployed owner (address owner) — the mutant that sends leftover balance to msg.sender can leave address(c).balance == 0 but cause owner to not receive funds, so checking owner is beneficiary distinguishes them.

For every admissible call to go by any caller sending any ETH, the contract's owner (the deployer) ends up with the ETH (address(c).balance == 0 and owner has increased balance via transfer) — the mutant that transfers to msg.sender can leave the owner not receiving the funds; we instead assert that address(c).balance == 0 after go() (reference always forwards remaining balance out, mutant can leave balance 0 as well but difference is recipient — instead assert that owner’s balance increases vs caller's? Since we cannot read external accounts' balances except via vm, we assert that calling go by the deployer leaves address(c).balance == 0 when the called target accepts or reverts appropriately).

For any caller and any payable amount sent to go(), the reference contract C always forwards its remaining balance to owner so that address(c).balance == 0 after a successful call; the mutant that removes the transfer can leave a non-zero contract balance for some inputs (amounts), violating this rule.

For every successful call to go() the reference contract always ends with its balance forwarded to owner (so address(c).balance == 0), while the mutant that removes the transfer can leave a positive contract balance for some inputs (when the callee consumes the forwarded value), so there exists an input where address(c).balance != 0.

For any admissible call where the external callee successfully accepts the forwarded msg.value but reclaims less than the sent amount (so C retains a positive balance before forwarding), the reference always forwards any remaining balance to owner leaving address(c).balance == 0; the mutant that removes the transfer can leave a positive contract balance, violating this.

For any caller and any payable amount, if the callee (target) consumes exactly the forwarded msg.value and then returns normally, the reference C will have zero balance after go() (it forwards any remaining balance to owner), whereas the mutant that deleted the final transfer can leave the contract with a non-zero balance for some inputs — specifically when the callee performs a reentrant call back into C that causes C to retain balance: therefore the rule is that after a successful go() invoked via a reentrant callee, address(c).balance == 0 for the reference but may be > 0 for the mutant.

For every successful call to C.go routed through an external callee that REVERTS the forwarded call (so C keeps some balance temporarily), the correct contract always forwards its remaining balance out leaving address(c).balance == 0, whereas the mutant that removed the final transfer can leave a positive balance (address(c).balance > 0) for some fuzzed payment amount and attacker address.
